newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller heralds Black Sea free trade plan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller heralds Black Sea free trade plan.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller heralded on Wednesday the plans of a Black Sea regional cooperation forum to establish a free trade zone in the region.
"I consider it very important that we have an agreement in principle on creating a free trade zone," Ciller said at a meeting of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation (BSEC) group.
"The infrastructure has been put in place to create a big trade area," she said. BSEC officials say it would take until 2010 to open such a free trade zone.

Speaking at a news conference following the meeting, Ciller said projects planned by the group would benefit from credit opportunities provided by the Black Sea Trade and Development Bank, set to open at the end of May in Thessaloniki, Greece.
"We will see in the near future new projects carried out with state incentives, but by the private sector," Ciller said.

Wednesday's talks were attended by foreign ministers or senior ministry officials from the 11 BSEC members -- Turkey, Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Georgia, Greece, Moldova, Romania, Russia and Ukraine.
The meeting was held at the end of a three-day conference of member countries.

Among those attending was Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos, who on Tuesday announced Greece would maintain a veto on European Union aid to Turkey. In talks with Ciller he said Greece would work with Turkey to improve the troubled relations between the two NATO members.

The Black Sea forum has unveiled plans for six regional cooperation projects focused on energy conservation, gas pipelines, development of small and medium enterprises, infrastructure, a project related to the use of the Danube River and another to speed border access in the region.
BSEC officials have said bilateral antagonism as well as the lack of a private sector in some member states and the troubled economies of ex-Soviet states, have slowed down the group.
BSEC, the brainchild of the late Turkish president Turgut Ozal, was set up in June 1992 in Istanbul.
The group has a secretariat in Istanbul, a parliamentary assembly, a private-sector business council, an economic data centre and several working bodies.

Six heads of state, ministers of transport, economy and communication, representatives of the World Bank, the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development and the International Finance Corporation, and some 600 businessmen were at the forum.
